tingle.whatBody: That tingly, fizzy feeling on your scalp or the back of your neck when you listen to ASMR. Everyone's tingles come from different sounds, so picking and stacking your own works best.

tingle.body: That tingly, fizzy feeling certain sounds give you

layered.body: Two sounds on top of each other. Just put one on the second row

noTalking.body: ASMR with sounds only, no speaking

s1.title: Shop
s1.body: Add blocks of the triggers you love (tapping, crinkles, whispers…). Free blocks are yours right away; paid ones have a 30-second preview.

s2.title: Build
s2.body: Tap your blocks to click them together. Hold and drag to place them anywhere, and layer two sounds with Layered.

s3.title: How long?
s3.body: Pick 30 minutes to 8 hours and save — we build one seamless track.

s4.title: Listen from Home
s4.body: Your combos are at the top of Home. Tap one to listen right away.

help.headline:
Stack your own <tingle/>
block by block
help.lead: One sound, one block. Pick the triggers you love — 3 minutes of tapping, 3 of crinkles, 3 of whispers — click them together, and you've got ASMR made just for you.
help.tip: ★ In Combos, listen to what others stacked and save the ones you like in one tap.

rec.headline: All you need is a phone
rec.lead: A quiet spot, a hand's width away, one clear trigger. Get these right and you'll have a block people love to hear.
rec.dontsNote: Please upload only sounds you recorded yourself. These are sent back in review, and can be taken down later if reported.
rec.endBody: Long recordings are fine — pick the best part from the waveform when you upload.
rec.readyMsg: Great — start recording. Stay quiet for the first 5 seconds!
rec.diagramA11y: Place the phone mic a hand's width, 15 to 20 centimeters, from the sound
